findings.text: the only assertion that the index actually answered is `0 < len(lookups.projects) <= len({FIRST, SECOND})`; a regression making _indexed_plan_states return {} for every project would send each ref to the _parsed_plan_state fallback, still make zero full reads and still call the index once, so every assertion stays green while each referenced plan is parsed from its own document instead of being read from the index the goal names — an assertion distinguishing the index hit from the fallback (e.g. counting _parsed_plan_state) would close it.

the live-vs-archived bucket in _indexed_plan_states silently prefers the live document when a slug has both copies, whereas _store._resolve_html_file documents that a genuine live-plus-archived pair raises a collision that must not be silently resolved, so a ref to a duplicated slug now reports found=true from the live copy where the base revision's read_plan raised and _resolve_plan_ref returned found=false; the docstring at reckon/mcp.py:1963 asserts the pick matches a full read's resolution, which is not true for that pair.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_plan_read_reads_each_referenced_plan_once.py:234 fails on the reinstated defect, as the negative control shows at EXIT=1, and :256 compares the rows against the real base-revision per-ref read rather than against the code under test; but :241 is the only assertion that the index answered, so a permanent index miss that fell through to _parsed_plan_state would leave the suite green.
justifications.evidence: the done_when's test tests/test_a_plan_read_reads_each_referenced_plan_once.py ran green at the reviewed head (52 passed, EXIT=0 in logs/head-arm.log) with a red negative control (1 failed, EXIT=1, four reads of first-target and two of second-target) in logs/negative-control.log; the manifest records no ruff result although the done_when names it, and I verified it clean myself.
justifications.fit: the three added helpers in reckon/mcp.py are named by what they do and the lazy `from reckon import metadata_index` matches the module's existing local-import idiom, but the docstring at reckon/mcp.py:1963 claims the live-first pick matches a full read's resolution, which _store._resolve_html_file contradicts for a live-plus-archived pair.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/mcp.py:1952 _indexed_plan_states answers every ref from one per-project index lookup and reckon/mcp.py:1991 _indexed_plan_state memoises it, so the reviewed read makes zero full reads of either referenced plan; the index build it triggers parses the project tree on a cold store, which is broader than the goal's wording but not a full read of a referenced plan.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses metadata_index.discovery_state as the owner of per-file parsed state and _store._resolve_html_file plus _plan_html.read_state_file for the miss path, adding no second parser or second plan reader; the only new mechanism is a per-read memo dict keyed by (project, checkout_path).
justifications.scope_discipline: the single commit e967d2ecc6 touches only reckon/mcp.py, tests/test_a_plan_read_reads_each_referenced_plan_once.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-read-costs-what-changed/read-costs-referenced-plan-once-s22.html, all inside the declared write paths; the declared figure path is unused and the metadata-index repair is recorded under outside_scope rather than made.
